title: The House of Garmu
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: They are mentioned in Mishnah Shekalim 5:1 as having been in charge, in the Second Temple, of making the showbread; and in Yoma 3:11, that they did not want to teach anyone how to make the showbread. In the Gemara there, 38a, they brought other craftsmen from Alexandria in Egypt, but they could not remove the loaves from the oven as they did; the House of Garmu would not return to their work until their wage was doubled. They said that the reason they did not want to teach anyone how to make the showbread was that they had a tradition from their fathers that the Temple was destined to be destroyed, and perhaps an unworthy person would learn it and go and serve idolatry with it. For this they are mentioned favorably: fine bread was never found in their children’s hands, so that people would not say that it was from the making of the showbread.

notes.text: רדות is removal of the loaves from the oven. The family’s refusal, double wage, future-idolatry concern and absence of fine bread from their children’s hands remain separate claims.
